key_insight: Train a cheaper, smaller model with RLVR first, then transfer the learned behavior directly to a stronger model through on-policy distillation. This weak-to-strong pipeline can reduce the cost of post-training while still improving reasoning performance.
problem_solved: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can improve language-model reasoning, but repeating RL on every new strong model is expensive because it requires many rollouts from the target model. The paper addresses the bottleneck of costly post-training as models scale.
method: Run RLVR on a smaller, cheaper "weak" model to learn useful reasoning behavior.
Reuse the post-RL policy data to distill those improvements into a stronger target model.
Use direct on-policy distillation so the strong model learns from the weak model's RL-optimized outputs instead of retraining RL from scratch.
impact: This approach offers a more practical path to scaling reasoning improvements across larger models without paying the full rollout cost each time. For practitioners, it suggests a cheaper way to transfer RL gains into production-grade models.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing weak model RLVR training flowing into strong model distillation.

paper_title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Shiyuan Feng, Huan-ang Gao, Haohan Chi, Hanlin Wu, Zhilong Zhang
